title: Tiny Tactics: a free Advance Wars-style tactics game you can play in your browser
author: Rovak
selftext:
I've been building **Tiny Tactics**, a turn-based tactics game in the spirit of Advance Wars, with a cute toy-soldier look. It's free, runs in your browser, and needs no download or account.

**What's in it**
- 5 story campaigns with 50 missions, from a gentle bootcamp to tough finales
- 6 voiced commanders, each with their own powers and personality
- Skirmish vs the CPU on 30+ maps, with three difficulty levels
- Online multiplayer: rated matches, leaderboards (global, country and seasonal) and replays
- Async games: take your turn whenever you like, with a notification when it's your move
- A map editor to build and share your own battlefields

Built with heavy help from AI tools for code, playtesting, art and voices.

▶️ Play: https://play.tinytactics.app
🌐 More info: https://tinytactics.app

I'd love to hear what you think, especially about the campaigns and the online play!

comments.author: maddix_cummings
comments.body: "In the spirit of Advance Wars" -> Makes Advance Wars

replies.author: Rovak
replies.body: Fair, It started as an experiment to see how hard it'd be to build a game with Opus 5.5, and Advance Wars seemed to be a relatively simple way to start. Actually I was inspired by [https://awbw.amarriner.com](https://awbw.amarriner.com) whichs seems to have a bit of an outdated look. The plan is to keep iterating until it's its own thing.

replies.author: maddix_cummings
replies.body: I mean it's not going to be hard to build something that's already been built dozens of time and that was not that technically advanced even back then. Most of AW's charm came from the story, art and characters. It's neither challenging you or Opus to build an Advance Wars clone.

replies.author: Rovak
replies.body: Well, now I know it's not hard, and I had fun doing it. Win-win 😄. Hopefully it inspires others to give it a shot as well.

comments.author: deReaLizedGames
comments.body: This looks so good! Love the art style, animations, and the UI. The trailer itself is really  well done too.  You should be really proud!!

replies.author: Rovak
replies.body: Thank you! I'm a bit torn on being proud with AI doing so much of the work. But ultimately steering it into a direction that turned into something fun was a nice learning experience.

replies.author: deReaLizedGames
replies.body: To be fair, if you look at the average AI game, they're half-baked prototypes. You built a full game that looks really well made. I'm sure that took much more time and effort compared to the average. We all know it's not as easy as "build x game entirely," it takes a lot of iteration and attention to detail. It's not that you didn't put in work, it's that you put in a different type of work to make the game. Give yourself some credit! :)

comments.author: waltergalvao
comments.body: Gotta teach sergeant poppy how to use a whistle (0:33) hahaha but that apart, looks fun! Good job

comments.author: TheMightyOscar
comments.body: Damn this actually looks very solid, how are you hosting the game and handling the multiplayer?

replies.author: Rovak
replies.body: Thanks! All Cloudflare: the client is a static site, and each match is a Durable Object (a tiny server per game) using WebSockets. The client and server share the same TypeScript game engine, so the server validates every move, and match history and ratings live in D1. Basically serverless, nearly free to run when it's quiet.

comments.author: vanidmt
comments.body: Advance Wars vibes in the browser with no download. The fact you fit 50 missions, 30+ maps, and a functional online ladder all into a single-file web experience is impressive.
